blocks.content: The minimum age requirement for constitutional office-holders varies across positions, while retirement ages specifically distinguish central and state judiciary and commissions.

items: High Court judges retire at 62 years, whereas Supreme Court judges retire at 65 years—frequently tested in match-the-following questions.
The tenure of the CAG and UPSC Chairman is 6 years or until 65 years of age, unlike political offices which typically have a 5-year tenure.
There is no upper age limit specified in the Indian Constitution for holding the office of President, Prime Minister, or Governor.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The minimum age requirement for the President, Vice-President, and State Governors is 35 years.
Members of the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies must be at least 25 years old, whereas Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council members must be at least 30 years old.
Supreme Court judges hold office until reaching 65 years of age, while High Court judges retire at 62 years.
Constitutional bodies like the UPSC and CAG feature a maximum tenure of 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
